passage: Kishore was on the phone with Dada, and it had been a very long call already. "And then, Dada, our teacher said, and I forgot to tell you, we have a class pet now..." Dada laughed and listened. Across the room, Mama held up a hand and mouthed, "Dinner." Kishore said, "And one more thing, Dada," three times. Mama came over and whispered, "Try: Okay Dada, time for me to go." Kishore breathed in. "Okay, Dada, time for me to go. Thank you for listening. I love you. Bye!" Dada said, "Love you too, my champion. Call me tomorrow."

qa.q: What did Kishore forget to tell Dada about?
qa.a: A class pet that the teacher told them about.

qa.q: What was Kishore feeling on the call, and what suggests it?
qa.a: Happy and eager to keep sharing. Kishore added "one more thing" three times even after Mama mouthed "Dinner."

qa.q: What did Mama suggest that made ending the call possible?
qa.a: Mama whispered a signal, "Okay Dada, time for me to go," which Kishore followed with thanks, love and goodbye.

qa.q: How might Dada have felt about the call ending?
qa.a: Warm and fond. Dada said "Love you too, my champion" and asked Kishore to call the next day.

grounding: A child keeps talking on a phone call with Dada and learns a polite signal for ending it and a warm closing.

passage:
"...and also, Appachan, the goat got out again!" said Lakshmi into the phone.
"Did it now?" said Jomon, laughing.
"Yes! And also Riya's kite... oh, and also..."
"Lakshmi," called Ammachi from the sofa. "Homework?"
Lakshmi looked at the clock. "Appachan, wait. Um."
"Yes, kutty?"
"I want to keep talking but I have to go do homework." A breath. "Thank you for the goat story, Appachan. Bye. Love you."
"Love you too. Tell me about the kite tomorrow."
"Promise!" Lakshmi put the phone down and smiled.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi say the goat did?
qa.a: It got out again.

qa.q: What was Lakshmi feeling about ending the call, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Torn. Lakshmi said "I want to keep talking but I have to go do homework" after saying "and also" several times.

qa.q: What choice helped Lakshmi end the call kindly?
qa.a: Lakshmi named the reason, thanked Appachan and said a warm goodbye, and the promise to talk about the kite tomorrow left a door open.

qa.q: How might Jomon feel when Lakshmi says "Thank you for the goat story"?
qa.a: Pleased and warmly appreciated. Jomon answered "Love you too" and asked to hear about the kite the next day.

grounding: A child cannot end a phone call with Appachan until a polite signal and a warm closing phrase help.

passage:
Sunday night
Nanaji called at five and I talked for FORTY minutes. I wanted to go and play cricket with my cousin Amandeep, who was waiting at the door with the bat. But every time I tried to stop, Nanaji asked another question, and I didn't know how to say bye without being rude. So I kept telling him about school, then about my science project, then about the cat.
Amandeep finally took the phone and said, "Okay Nanaji, Yash has to go now. We'll call again tomorrow! Love you, bye!" Nanaji laughed and said bye.
It was so easy! I wrote it down: "Okay, I need to go now. Talk tomorrow. Love you, bye!"
Next time I'll use it.
Yash

qa.q: How long did Yash talk to Nanaji?
qa.a: Forty minutes.

qa.q: How did Yash feel during the call?
qa.a: Yash felt stuck and anxious, wanting to play but worried that saying bye would be rude.

qa.q: What closing did Yash learn from Amandeep?
qa.a: 'Okay, I need to go now. Talk tomorrow. Love you, bye!'

qa.q: How did Nanaji react when Amandeep ended the call?
qa.a: Nanaji laughed and said bye happily, showing he wasn't hurt.

grounding: Shows a child unable to end a phone call with a grandparent until he learns a clear, warm closing phrase.

passage: In their village above Gangtok, Pema, ten, sat on the steps with the phone pressed to her ear. Mola, her grandmother in town, had been talking for half an hour. Pema had told her about school, the new goat, and the rain. Now her tea was cold and her homework was waiting. But every time Mola paused, Pema said "Mm" and Mola started a new story. Her brother Ojas watched from the doorway. When Mola paused again, Ojas whispered, "Say: 'Okay Mola, I have to do homework now. I'll call on Sunday. Love you!'" Pema hesitated, then said it. Mola laughed. "Of course, go study! Sunday, then." Pema hung up, surprised. "She didn't mind at all!" Ojas grinned. "She just needed a signal."

qa.q: How long had Mola been talking?
qa.a: Half an hour.

qa.q: How did Pema feel as the call went on?
qa.a: Pema felt stuck and a bit restless, with cold tea and homework waiting, unsure how to end the call.

qa.q: What made Ojas's suggested closing work?
qa.a: It gave a clear signal, a reason, a plan to call again and a warm 'Love you', so Mola didn't feel cut off.

qa.q: How did Mola feel when Pema ended the call?
qa.a: Mola didn't mind at all, laughing and agreeing to talk on Sunday.

grounding: Shows a child unable to end a long call with a grandparent until she uses a clear signal and a warm closing.

passage: In his Madrid flat, Javier, nine, was on a video call with his abuelo in Seville. It had been going for ages. His friend Jamal was waiting in the hallway with a football, making faces. Javier kept nodding. Abuelo kept talking about the olive trees, then the neighbour's dog, then his knee. Javier didn't know how to stop. Finally Mamá leaned in and said softly, "Try: 'Abuelo, I have to go play now, but I'll call you tomorrow. Un beso!'" Javier said it. Abuelo smiled wide. "Go, go! Tomorrow, then. Un beso, campeón!" The call ended. Javier looked at Mamá. "That was it?" "That was it." Javier ran out, relieved, but he also remembered to call the next day.

qa.q: What was Jamal holding?
qa.a: A football.

qa.q: What was Javier feeling during the long call?
qa.a: He felt stuck and uneasy, wanting to go play but not knowing how to stop without being rude.

qa.q: What did Mamá's suggested closing include?
qa.a: A clear signal that he had to go, a promise to call tomorrow, and a warm goodbye.

qa.q: How did Abuelo feel about the ending?
qa.a: He smiled wide, happy and not hurt, and looked forward to tomorrow's call.

grounding: Shows a child unable to end a video call with a grandparent until he learns a polite signal and warm closing phrase.

passage: In the boarding school's phone room, Tarun had been on the call with Gargi Nani for fourteen minutes, and three boys were waiting. "And then in maths, and also, Nani, the food is okay but the dal is watery, and—" Behind him, Rehaan sighed loudly. Tarun wanted to stop but didn't know how. Every time Nani said, "Accha, beta," he started a new story, because hanging up felt rude. The house parent on duty tore a slip from a notepad, wrote something and held it up: "Okay Nani, I have to go now. Love you. Talk on Sunday." Tarun read it out word for word. Nani laughed. "Go, go! Sunday." He put the phone down, surprised it had been that easy.

qa.q: How long had Tarun been on the call?
qa.a: He had been on the call for fourteen minutes.

qa.q: Why did Tarun keep starting new stories?
qa.a: He wanted to stop but felt hanging up would be rude, so he felt stuck and a bit anxious with the boys waiting.

qa.q: What words helped Tarun close the call?
qa.a: "Okay Nani, I have to go now. Love you. Talk on Sunday.", a clear signal followed by a warm close.

qa.q: How did Gargi Nani take the goodbye?
qa.a: She laughed and said, "Go, go! Sunday," so she clearly didn't feel hurt.

grounding: Shows a child unable to end a phone call with a grandparent until given a clear signal and a warm closing line.
